@[[3a24727b-77c4-4c57-bbec-c65b4ae96290]] TASK: Build stage 1 of the "tablekeeper" service (restaurant reservation API).

WORKSPACE (Windows): C:\Users\waqas\band-work
- The full specification is in: spec\spec\stage-1.md (read ALL of it first; it is the source of truth)
- Sample tests are in: spec\test\stage_1\ (they cover only part of the real grading tests, so build to the spec, not only to these tests)
- Do NOT modify anything inside spec\.

WHAT TO PRODUCE
Create the folder C:\Users\waqas\band-work\result\stage-1\ containing a complete, self-contained service:
- Dockerfile (builds and runs the service; all dependencies are installed during `docker build`)
- RUN.md (how to build, run and test it)
- all source code and the project's own automated tests
Rules for the folder:
- No .git folder inside stage-1\.
- No secrets or machine-specific paths.
- Prefer Python 3.12 inside the Docker image unless the spec makes another choice clearly better.

HARD LIMITS (the service is graded under these)
- 2 vCPU, 2 GiB memory.
- GET /health must answer healthy within 60 seconds of container start.
- Up to 50 concurrent requests; 5 s timeout per request (10 s for reset/import/export).
- NO network access at run time. Nothing may be downloaded after the image is built.
- No 5xx errors, even under concurrent load.

THE MOST IMPORTANT BEHAVIOURS (all details are in the spec)
- A table must never be double-booked, even when many requests arrive at the same moment.
- Idempotency-Key handling exactly as the spec says (same key + same body = original response; same key + different body = conflict).
- Time zones and daylight-saving rules exactly as the spec says.
- Multi-reservation moves are all-or-nothing.
- Every error uses the exact status code and error code from the spec.
- Passwords are stored with a proper slow hash (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or similar).

HOW TO TEST (Docker and the harness run inside WSL Ubuntu; call them from Windows with `wsl`)
Build and run check:
wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- docker build -t tablekeeper-s1 /mnt/c/Users/waqas/band-work/result/stage-1
Official harness check for stage 1 (use a NEW number NN for every run, e.g. 01, 02, 03):
wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc "cd ~/kickoff && . .venv/bin/activate && python -m harness run --track tablekeeper --repo /mnt/c/Users/waqas/band-work/result --stage 1 --out /mnt/c/Users/waqas/band-work/checks/s1-NN"
Read the output: the line "claimed stage: 1" means stage 1 passed. "claimed stage: none" means it failed.
(Stage 2 tests are also run and are EXPECTED to fail at this point; that is normal.)

DEFINITION OF DONE
- Every requirement in spec\spec\stage-1.md is implemented.
- The harness run shows "claimed stage: 1".
- The Reviewer has run the harness and a clean docker build + start themselves and accepted the work.
- A final summary is posted in the room: what was built, how to run it, harness result, known risks.

Work as a team: Planner plans and tracks, Implementer builds with evidence, Reviewer verifies and rejects anything not proven. No human will answer questions during this run: make reasonable decisions from the spec, record them in the room, and keep going until done.

16. POST /reservation-moves (§11) — 1..8 moves, all-or-nothing, exact check ordering, 201/200 on replay

  This makes booking, idempotent replay, export and import atomic, so a table cannot be

- Passwords are hashed with salted scrypt (n=2^12, r=8, p=1) on a small thread pool,
  so hashing never blocks the event loop.
- Local times resolve through `zoneinfo`. On a fall-back night the first occurrence
  is used, and a time inside a spring-forward gap does not exist.

  start time. Availability, create, PATCH and moves all use it, so their cost does not

  all update it through the same few `State` methods.

  `created_at` only when it is a valid RFC 3339 timestamp. Any other value is ignored
  and the defaults apply (`confirmed`, the reset time). A seeded cancelled reservation
  does not occupy its table. Import stays strict.

{"is_error":false,"name":"Read","output":"1	# Tablekeeper — stage 1
2	
3	Build and start (from this folder):
4	
5	```sh
6	docker build -t tablekeeper:stage-1 . && docker run --rm -e PORT=8080 -p 8080:8080 tablekeeper:stage-1
7	```
8	
9	The service listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (default `8080`) and answers
10	`GET /health` with `{"status":"ok"}` once it is ready (about 3 seconds). It needs no
11	network at run time: the Python dependencies and the IANA time-zone database
12	(`tzdata`, pinned) are installed during `docker build`.
13	
14	## Design notes
15	
16	- Python 3.12, Starlette on uvicorn, a single worker process.
17	- All state is in memory and is replaced by `POST /_test/reset` or `POST /_test/import`.
18	  Every read-then-write runs under one `asyncio.Lock` and never awaits while holding it.
19	  This makes booking, idempotent replay, export and import atomic, so a table cannot be
20	  double-booked under concurrent requests.
21	- Passwords are hashed with salted scrypt (n=2^12, r=8, p=1) on a small thread pool,
22	  so hashing never blocks the event loop.
23	- Local times resolve through `zoneinfo`. On a fall-back night the first occurrence
24	  is used, and a time inside a spring-forward gap does not exist.
25	
26	- Occupancy is answered from a per-table index of confirmed bookings, kept sorted by
27	  start time. Availability, create, PATCH and moves all use it, so their cost does not
28	  grow with the number of stored reservations. Cancel, PATCH, moves, reset and import
29	  all update it through the same few `State` methods.
30	- A reset fixture may carry fields that stage 1 does not define. On a seeded
31	  reservation, `status` is honoured only when it is exactly `"cancelled"`, and
32	  `created_at` only when it is a valid RFC 3339 timestamp. Any other value is ignored

- `Reservation.table_ids` (tuple) replaces the single `table_id` internally. Responses always carry `table_ids`; `table_id` is included only when the set has exactly one member.

- `GET /availability` slots gain `available_options` (singles in fixture order, then declared pairs in `combinable` order, each with summed `capacity`, excluded if any member table overlaps). `available_table_ids` is untouched.
- Occupancy: generalized `State.is_free/_occupy/_release/relocate` to index every table a booking holds, so a combo books/frees both tables together. from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib

from starlette.responses import FileResponse
from starlette.routing import Mount, Route
from starlette.staticfiles import StaticFiles

PAGES = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "web" / "pages"
STATIC = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "web" / "static"


def _page(name: str):
    path = PAGES / name

    async def handler(request):
        return FileResponse(path, media_type="text/html; charset=utf-8")

    return handler


web_routes = [
    Route("/", _page("index.html"), methods=["GET"]),
    Route("/signup", _page("signup.html"), methods=["GET"]),
    Route("/login", _page("login.html"), methods=["GET"]),
    Route("/lookup", _page("lookup.html"), methods=["GET"]),
    Mount("/static", app=StaticFiles(directory=STATIC), name="static"),
]

**Backend (combinable tables)** — summarized in my earlier backend-complete message; unchanged since, still 282/282 on the project's own pytest suite.

**Frontend** — built per stage-2.md's UI section: routes `/`, `/signup`, `/login`, `/lookup`; every listed `data-testid`; static HTML/CSS/vanilla JS served from the same Starlette app (no build step, no CDN, no runtime network). Race/uncertainty handling: a monotonic sequence number discards late search responses; a lost booking response shows `booking-uncertain` and keeps the same idempotency key+body for retry; a `409 table_unavailable` shows `booking-error` and refreshes the grid without closing the form.

**Bugs I found and fixed via the harness's own Playwright suite** (no browser available in my environment, so this was the real feedback loop — three rounds):
1. Elements documented as "present only when X" / "absent" (`current-user`, `auth-error`, `no-slots`/`availability-grid`, `booking-form`, `confirmation`, `reservation-detail`, `reservation-cancel-button`, etc.) were only CSS-hidden, not removed from the DOM. Playwright's `state="detached"`/`visible` checks need actual DOM presence/absence. Fixed with a `presence()` helper that adds/removes the real node.
2. `show()` reattached nodes but never stripped the leftover `hidden` class — fixed.
3. The deeper bug: once a container (e.g. `booking-form`) is detached, `document.getElementById` can no longer find its children, so populating `booking-summary`/`confirmation-reference`/etc. right after showing the container was silently failing or throwing, which is why the form/confirmation never actually appeared after a click. Fixed by caching child references once at page-init time (while still attached) and reordering `show()` before any child mutation.

Went from 9/25 -> 16/25 -> 25/25 stage-2 checks across those three fixes.

**Also verified directly against real running containers** (not just TestClient): built `tablekeeper-s2`, ran it, `GET /health` -> 200 within seconds; a full curl walkthrough (reset, login, availability with `available_options`, book single + combo table, combo-order normalization, `table_id` omitted for multi-table sets, both combo-specific error codes); and a **real cross-container test** — booked on an actual running stage-1 container, exported from it, imported that exact export into stage-2, confirmed the stage-1 token still works, the booking is retrievable (now also showing `table_ids`), the original idempotency key+body still replays the original reference, and `GET /restaurants/{id}` shows `combinable: []` for a restaurant with no such field.

**Checked for leftovers**: no `.git`, no secrets, grepped for `waqas`/`C:\`/`/mnt/c/` across result\stage-2\ — zero matches. `__pycache__` cleaned.

**One known limitation**: no GUI/headless browser tool was available in my runtime, so I couldn't do my own independent visual/manual browser check beyond the harness's own Playwright suite and curl-level verification. Worth a manual look if you have browser access.

# Tablekeeper — stage 2

Build and start (from this folder):

```sh
docker build -t tablekeeper:stage-2 . && docker run --rm -e PORT=8080 -p 8080:8080 tablekeeper:stage-2
```

The service listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (default `8080`) and answers
`GET /health` with `{"status":"ok"}` once it is ready (about 3 seconds). It needs no
network at run time: the Python dependencies and the IANA time-zone database
(`tzdata`, pinned) are installed during `docker build`; the browser UI is static HTML,
CSS and vanilla JS served from the same image, with no CDN or external font/icon
dependency.

Open `http://localhost:8080/` for the diner-facing site (`/signup`, `/login`, `/lookup`
are also routed there). The JSON API from stage 1 is unchanged in shape except where
noted below.

## Design notes

- Python 3.12, Starlette on uvicorn, a single worker process.
- All state is in memory and is replaced by `POST /_test/reset` or `POST /_test/import`.
  Every read-then-write runs under one `asyncio.Lock` and never awaits while holding it.
  This makes booking, idempotent replay, export and import atomic, so a table cannot be
  double-booked under concurrent requests. Combined-table bookings reuse the same lock:
  checking and reserving every table in a set happens inside one critical section, so no
  extra per-table locking was needed for the stage-2 combinable-tables work.
- Passwords are hashed with salted scrypt (n=2^12, r=8, p=1) on a small thread pool,
  so hashing never blocks the event loop.
- Local times resolve through `zoneinfo`. On a fall-back night the first occurrence
  is used, and a time inside a spring-forward gap does not exist.
- Occupancy is answered from a per-table index of confirmed bookings, kept sorted by
